Subject: Follow-up: latency targets & streaming needs (TTFT)

Thanks again for the demo earlier — helpful discussion. A few follow-ups from our side so we can scope the pilot correctly: 

• Business targets: for interactive patient-facing flows we need Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) at the 95th percentile to be <= 100ms for short prompts (~<64 tokens). For longer flows (multi-turn notes) 95p <= 200ms is acceptable.

• Traffic profile: steady concurrency of ~60 sessions (concurrent active streams), expected peak spikes up to ~180 concurrent sessions for 10-15 minute windows. Typical request size is 16–256 tokens; ~60% of requests are sub-64 tokens.

• Streaming: mobile/web clients prefer server-sent events (SSE) for simplicity. Desired chunk cadence is ~100ms per chunk for real-time feel, but we can tolerate up to 250ms if TTFT remains low. Ability to switch to WebSocket if we need bi-directional or lower overhead is a plus.

• Fallbacks & reliability: if model variant or region is saturated we need graceful fallback to a slightly lower-capacity model with clearly documented latency impact.

Can you confirm these targets are reasonable for a 4-week pilot and provide a suggested pilot config (instance types / concurrency limits / expected throughput) and what metrics you’ll collect? Also send a sample test harness we can run against pre-prod.

Thanks,
Ayesha
Senior Product Manager — Nimbus Health

Ayesha — great to connect. Recap and proposed next steps below.

Recap of targets you provided:
- TTFT 95p <= 100ms for short prompts (<64 tokens); TTFT 95p <= 200ms for long flows — confirmed.
- Sustained concurrency ~60; peak ~180.
- SSE preferred; fallback to WebSocket if required.

Suggested 4-week pilot scope (high level):
1) Week 0: Pilot kickoff + access provisioning (VPC peering or test API key).
2) Week 1: Baseline run — sample harness to replay representative traffic (we’ll provide). Collect TTFT, latency distribution, token throughput, and CPU/GPU utilization.
3) Week 2: Tuning — batching/kv-cache and chunk cadence adjustments to hit TTFT targets under sustained traffic.
4) Week 3: Peak testing — simulate 180 concurrent sessions in burst windows; validate fallbacks.
5) Week 4: Wrap & SOW/next steps (SLA, pricing, Dedicated sizing).

Pilot config proposal (initial):
- Hosted trial on 4 x A100-like instances (shared) behind our smart router with autoscale headroom; if you prefer dedicated we can size Dedicated pool (recommended for predictable p95).
- Initial concurrency cap per-instance to keep per-token latency stable; we’ll provide exact numbers after first baseline run.

Metrics we’ll deliver: TTFT (p50/p95/p99), per-chunk timing, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, queue depth, and error/retry counts. We’ll also provide a CSV of sample results.

Next steps: please confirm the pilot start week and whether you prefer Hosted (faster) or Dedicated (predictable). I’ll loop in Karthik for the technical runbook and load harness.

Cheers,

Ayesha, Vivek — adding a technical note so we’re aligned before baseline: 

Quick thoughts to hit TTFT 95p <= 100ms for short prompts: 
- Warm KV-cache / prefix caching: for interactive UIs we can aggressively cache model KV for common prefixes (system prompts) which drops TTFT significantly. If your clients use deterministic system prompts this will help a lot.
- Initial token chunking: send the first chunk with the smallest possible token window (e.g., 8–12 tokens) to minimize the server-side model compute before the first bytes are flushed. That alone often reduces TTFT by 20–40ms vs waiting for a 64-token chunk.
- Chunk cadence vs size trade-offs: target cadence ~80–140ms and chunk sizes ~12–48 tokens for the mobile use-case you described. For higher throughput server-to-server flows we can increase token window and cadence (200–300ms).
- SSE vs WebSocket: SSE simplifies client reconnection and scales well for one-way streaming. If you need fine-grained backpressure or multiplexing we recommend WebSocket. The pilot can use SSE; we’ll instrument both endpoints and compare overhead.
- Backpressure & concurrency: implement client-side concurrency knobs (max inflight per session) and a request-level timeout fallback to a non-streaming fast-path.

I’ve attached a short diagram of the streaming topology and a sample load script.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

2) Chunk cadence: we’ll try SSE with a 100ms cadence for the mobile client during the pilot. If results show GC/overhead issues we can relax to 200ms.
3) Test harness: please send the harness + a sample traffic file that mirrors our 60 sustained / 180 peak scenario. We’ll run it against your pre-prod.
4) Data security: we need to confirm data handling — are logs redacted by default and what retention window applies for pilot keys? (Marissa, can you add the security contact to the thread?)
